dedupe_keys.name: discrete event simulation of tank truck loading operations in a fuel distribution terminal reis pitombeira neto and rolim ijsimm 2017

description: This record describes a discrete-event simulation model of tank truck loading in a fuel distribution terminal, published in the International Journal of Simulation Modelling in 2017 by researchers at the Federal University of Ceara and the fuel distributor Raizen in Brazil. The model covers truck arrivals, fuel demand generation and truck scheduling, and the authors propose a decomposition of the joint probability distribution of correlated fuel demands and a queuing policy that considers the current state of the terminal. It was validated against the performance indicators of a real terminal, then used to test higher fuel flow rates, more loading arms and the new policy, which lowered idleness and lead time compared with first-come-first-served. Access: the paper PDF is free to download from the journal site; no code or data files are mentioned and no licence is stated in the text. Coverage is one terminal. Caveats: the simulation software is not named in the text sections read, and only the abstract, introduction and conclusion were reviewed. It suits capacity planning and optimisation studies of fuel distribution terminals, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
